speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; to begin our evaluation, have you noticed any trauma, insect bites, or recent exposure to plants in that area? Additionally, does the pain radiate up your arm or cause your entire hand to become red and warm?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That sounds like a significant jam injury to your finger; given the mechanism of injury and the progressive swelling two days later, did you notice any specific deformity of the finger or experience a loud "pop" at the moment of impact?

Also, can you tell me if the swelling is localized to the joint or extends up the finger, and have you had any difficulty bending or straightening it?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (extensor tendon avulsion). The combination of a forced flexion injury (jersey pull), pain at the DIP joint, inability to flex the DIP joint, and the finger remaining extended in rest confirms avulsion of the extensor tendon from the distal phalanx.
